sections.title: Context and result types
sections.what: Defines the case context the adapter reads and a result wrapper that carries the source name, a synthetic flag, the data and a disclaimer.
sections.why: Makes every answer visibly marked as demo data.

sections.name: GovernmentAdapter
sections.title: Adapter contract
sections.what: Lists the three methods every government adapter must provide: status, survey record, and available actions, each returning the wrapper.
sections.why: Keeps any future real adapter in the same shape as the mock.

sections.name: MockGovernmentAdapter, mockGovernmentAdapter
sections.title: Mock adapter and shared instance
sections.what: Implements the three methods with fixed synthetic answers and not-official disclaimers, and exports one shared instance. The status answer uses the workflow stage. The actions answer states that nothing can be submitted from the app.
sections.why: Gives demo screens realistic-looking data without any real connection.
sections.watch_out: The mock returns the case's own stage name as the status, so it reflects demo data rather than a real government record.

summary: Defines the rules for a government data adapter and a mock version that returns fixed, clearly labelled synthetic answers about a case's survey status, record and allowed actions.
purpose: Lets the app show survey status and actions for demos without connecting to any government system, and sets a clear pattern for any real integration later.
why: Likely reason: integration with official systems is not yet approved, so only a mock exists. The code comment says future integrations must use documented, authorized interfaces.
how: The mock reads the case's stage, survey record and parcels, then returns each answer wrapped in a result that states its source, that it is synthetic, and a disclaimer. The actions list comes from the workflow stage.
inputs: Case context: the case, its survey record and its land parcels.
outputs: Wrapped results for status, record and available actions.
risks: The disclaimers are the only thing that tells users the data is not official. The mock never submits anything, and that rule is written into the disclaimer text.
debug: If an answer looks official, check the disclaimer and synthetic flag in the mock. If the stage is wrong, check the stage name passed to the workflow resolver.
